---
title: "Export SVG contract"
---

The contract between `make export` (this repository) and downstream tools such as [papercraft-nester](https://github.com/tungufoss/papercraft-nester) ([converter issue #17](https://github.com/tungufoss/lowpoly-pdf-to-svg/issues/17), [nester issue #12](https://github.com/tungufoss/papercraft-nester/issues/12)). Version **`lowpoly-export/1`**. A consumer reads only what is listed here: `data-*` attributes, element names, `d`, `x`, `y` and `transform`. Styles, `inkscape:label`, layer nesting and element order are presentation and may change without a version bump.

The review SVG (`<project>.svg`) is **not** covered: it is work in progress and keeps the PDF numbers. Consume only `<project>-export.svg`.

## Document

| Where | Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<svg>` | `data-contract` | `lowpoly-export/1`. Reject other values. |
| `<svg>` | `data-units` | `mm`: every coordinate (`viewBox`, `d`, `x`, `y`) is in millimetres. |
| `<svg>` | `width`, `height` | Physical size in inches (`in`), equal to the `viewBox` size / 25.4, so Inkscape and Cricut Design Space open it at true scale. |
| `<svg>` | `data-project` | Model name from the YAML. |

`<inkscape:page>` elements inside `sodipodi:namedview` show the source pages; they are informational.

## Piece

Every physical paper piece is one `<g data-piece="…">`. Find pieces by that attribute anywhere in the tree, not by layer.

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `data-piece` | Stable unique id, `piece-PP-NN` (source page, piece number on the page). Same as the group's `id`. |
| `data-material` | Cardstock id from the YAML (`red`, `black`, …). Pieces with the same id go on the same sheets. |
| `data-material-name` | Human name, e.g. `Red cardstock`. |
| `data-color` | Cardstock colour as `#rrggbb` (YAML `color:`). |
| `data-source-pdf` | Source PDF file name. |
| `data-source-page` | 1-based PDF page the piece was traced from. |
| `data-page-origin-mm` | `x y` of that page's top-left corner in document mm; subtract it to get PDF page coordinates. |

A piece group and every group inside it has **no `transform`**. A nester places a piece by wrapping or setting a transform on the piece group itself.

## Operations

Every drawable element inside a piece is a `<path>` or `<text>` carrying `data-operation`:

| `data-operation` | Element | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `cut` | `<path>` | Exactly one per piece: the cut boundary. One compound path, outline first then any holes, closed polygons (`M x,y x,y … Z`, straight segments only), filled with `fill-rule:evenodd`. |
| `score` | `<path>` | One straight fold line `M x,y x,y`, with `data-fold` = `mountain` or `valley`. |
| `draw` | `<text>` | One pen label or piece number, see below. |
| `draw` | `<path>` | The circle, square or underline of a piece number (`data-mark`), an open polyline. |

Coordinates in `d` are absolute, comma-separated pairs; no relative commands, arcs or curves. No `clipPath`, `mask`, `use`, `symbol` or `image` appears anywhere in the file.

## Labels

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| text content, `data-label` | The short label, e.g. `2A`. Same on both edges of a glue pair, used by no other edge. At least one letter; no 0/O, 1/I, Q, 6, 9. |
| `data-pdf-number` | The number printed in the PDF, for tracing back. |
| `data-pair-status` | Edge-check result for the pair: `ok`, `unpaired`, `length mismatch`, … (`ok` means two edges of matching length). |
| `data-edge` | `tab` (glue tab fold) or `edge` (plain cut edge), from the edge table; absent if the number had no row. |
| `x`, `y`, `transform` | Label centre in mm, and `rotate(angle x y)` only. |

Each label stands centred on the edge it marks (or spread along it when the edge carries two),
its baseline along the edge, inside the cut outline. A tab label sits on the tab and reads from
the tab's outer edge, its top towards the fold; if the tab has no room it goes on the piece side
of the fold. A label whose spot is taken by another label slides along its edge; as a last resort
it may stick out past the outline, but labels never cover each other. Every label has the same
`font-size`, `--label-size` (default 5 mm); the pen font's cap height is 0.75 of it.

## Piece numbers

Every piece also gets a `<text data-operation="draw" data-piece-number="N" data-label="N">` at
its widest inside point, clear of the outline and every label (fold lines may cross it), up to
`--number-size` (default 10 mm). Pieces are numbered 1, 2, … in piece order; mirror twins (from `mirror-mismatches.csv`)
share a number, the first with a circle round it and the second with a square
(`<path data-mark="circle|square">`). Numbers that read differently upside down (6, 9, 16, 69, …)
are underlined (`data-mark="underline"`). Piece numbers are not glue labels and never count as
one.

`<project>-labels.csv` holds the same mapping: `label, pdf_number, status, pieces`.

Complete glue pairs whose two edges belong to the same physical piece use a single
letter (`A`–`A`, then `B`–`B`, etc.). These letters are unique across the export and
come from the same pen-safe alphabet as other labels. Joins between separate pieces
keep their existing two-character (or longer) labels and sequence positions.
Incomplete or ambiguous edge groups keep their normal labels. An export containing
more self-joins than the alphabet has letters fails explicitly rather than reusing
a letter and making the pair ambiguous. Existing exported files are unchanged.

For cardstock already cut, set `export.frozen_labels: frozen-green/manifest.json`
in the project YAML (path relative to that YAML). The JSON `labels` list contains
`piece_id`, `pdf_number`, `edge` (`tab` or `edge`), and `label` for **every** printed
edge on the cut pieces. These labels override automatic assignment, including
self-joins, and propagate to the matching edge on another piece. Their labels are
reserved so new pairs cannot collide with them. Missing edges, conflicting labels,
and ambiguous identities fail before writing an export. Freeze the original SVG
and cut files alongside this manifest for provenance; never regenerate those files.

## Not provided yet

Body/tab boundaries are not in the export: the converter knows which numbered edge is a tab (`data-edge="tab"`) but not the tab's polygon, so a consumer must not infer one from the cut outline.

## Checking

`python -m src.lowpoly_pdf_to_svg.export --check FILE` lists every way a file breaks this contract (exit 1) or confirms it. `make export-check` rebuilds the synthetic fixture in `fixtures/export/` and fails if the export or the check changes; `fixtures/export/sample-export.svg` is a small file downstream tools can test against.
